slides.title: There's a Lesson in That
bullets: Prepare to read, discuss and write
slides.narration: Welcome to Grade 6 English, Unit 1: There's a Lesson in That. In this unit you will explore the world of fables — short stories that teach us important lessons about life. Fables have been told for thousands of years, passed from generation to generation by storytellers, teachers, and parents. They often use animal characters or simple human figures to show us truths about honesty, courage, kindness, and wisdom. As you work through this lesson, you will read a fable, answer questions about it, learn an important grammar rule called the Present Perfect Tense, and even write your own fable with a clear moral message. Every section builds on the one before it, so take your time and enjoy the journey. In this short lecture, preview the key ideas and prepare for the independent lesson.

slides.title: What you will achieve
bullets: Explain what a fable is and identify its key features, including characters, setting, problem, and moral
Read a fable closely and identify the moral or lesson it teaches
Use vocabulary related to governance, justice, community, and storytelling confidently in your own sentences
slides.narration: By the end of this unit, you will be able to explain what a fable is and identify its key features, including characters, setting, problem, and moral. You will also read a fable closely and identify the moral or lesson it teaches. You will also use vocabulary related to governance, justice, community, and storytelling confidently in your own sentences. Keep these goals in mind as you work.

slides.title: Language for precise thinking
slides.narration: Your vocabulary work begins with these words: accommodate, accommodation, amateur, attached, protagonist, admittedly. Listen to each pronunciation in the vocabulary lab, study its meaning in context, and use the word accurately in your own discussion and writing.

slides.title: Read critically
bullets: The Weaver and the Wind, part 1
The Weaver and the Wind, part 2
slides.narration: The reading sequence includes The Weaver and the Wind, part 1 and The Weaver and the Wind, part 2. Read actively. Identify each text's central ideas, notice viewpoint and reliability, and support every inference with relevant evidence from the text.

slides.title: What the Present Perfect Tense Shows
bullets: The present perfect links the past to the present. We use it for life experiences, recent news, and situations that began earlier and still matter now,...
slides.narration: The first language focus is What the Present Perfect Tense Shows. The present perfect links the past to the present. We use it for life experiences, recent news, and situations that began earlier and still matter now, without saying exactly when they happened. Notice the structure in the model examples, then apply it deliberately in connected sentences and paragraphs.

slides.title: Use English for a real purpose
bullets: Speaking 1: Retell a Fable from Memory
Writing 1: Plan and Write Your Own Fable
Explain, support and improve your ideas
slides.narration: In speaking, you will complete Speaking 1: Retell a Fable from Memory. Organise your ideas, use evidence and respond clearly to questions. In writing, you will plan, draft, check and revise. Use the success criteria before submitting your work.

slides.title: You are ready to begin
bullets: Activities, quiz and optional live sessions
slides.narration: You are ready to begin. Start with the vocabulary lab, continue through reading and comprehension, apply the grammar focus, and complete the speaking and writing practices. Use the AI tutor for hints and feedback any time, and bring your questions to a live session too if you join one.
